content: Albendazole, marketed under the brand name ALBENZA, is an orally administered broad-spectrum anthelmintic medication. Chemically, it is identified as methyl 5-(propylthio)-2-benzimidazolecarbamate, with the molecular formula C12H15N3O2S. The compound is characterized by a specific chemical structure. Albendazole appears as a white to off-white powder. It is soluble in dimethyl sulfoxide, strong acids, and strong bases. It exhibits slight solubility in methanol, chloroform, ethyl acetate, and acetonitrile. However, it is practically insoluble in water. Each film-coated tablet of Albendazole, which is white to off-white in color, contains 200 mg of the active ingredient. The formulation also includes several inactive ingredients: carnauba wax, hypromellose, lactose monohydrate, magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, povidone, sodium lauryl sulfate, sodium saccharin, sodium starch glycolate, and starch.
